Infinite fun
07/12/2020
Blah blah game boy

Before I start I want to point out that I’ve actually only ever played the Knight story in the Fantasy setting. This being said, I’ve still played this game for hours upon hours! It’s just so fun! The ai has so many different events at its disposal that in the many hours I’ve spent playing, I’ve never once seen the same event twice, aside from the beginning. The main story is always the same. Although you really don’t need to do the story. I’ve had the most fun just going out and doing whatever path the random events set me on.I will say the game isn’t perfect. Like I said I’ve only played the fantasy story, which is of course a medieval setting, but sometimes the ai seems to forget this and tells me I found a shotgun or a rifle. Sometimes in the middle of a fight it’ll say I pull out a gun and shoot whatever I’m fighting. Another problem is the ai having characters you’ve never met apparently with you and talking to you. One of the more absurd examples I’ve had is, after killing a werewolf, my mom started talking to me. There was no mention of her, I had never met them, let alone brought them with me. All of this is pretty uncommon but it can throw off your immersion and sometimes be a bit annoying. All in all I won’t complain too much because the devs are constantly updating and improving the game, so I’m sure they’ll fix it.

A Few Small Faulty Wires
02/03/2020
Oofadoodledum

The game can be very creative, but only if you work with the given genres. Genres like romance and general horror or thiller, or genres containing existential issues need a lot of clarity. And although the /remember tool is useful you need to use it a lot initially to keep the rules of the game consistent. But even then the game may forget it completely or force the rules onto the game so hard that personalities and events are unable to be changed. It isn’t like you can use /remember like a switch. Sometime the A.I. will completely not use key elements you used in the plot initiation. Another annoyance is that the game will interpret the proper grammar usage of “me, mine, my, etc.” as a new character which makes it feel like your talking to the game engine, completely disrupting any immersion. Despite this, the A.I. can be fairly creative if your vocabulary is expansive. And the potential and sheer amount of unique responses from the engine outcompetes any other app or game in this market. And third person pronoun usage is almost always correctly connected to the antecedents. Fixing the game to make it understand both complex and casual grammar and sentence structure is my general request/tip, but so far the only issues I’ve found have been very minor, though they produce a complex web of issues to the players. Honestly, the best thing about this app is that it’s free without any advertisements.

An overall fun but buggy experience
03/11/2024
MythicHex

I just picked up AI Dungeon on iOS a few days ago. If you’re patient and work within the limitations of AI, it works really well. It has the potential to give a modest stimulating experience, but you have to be willing to give back. So far, I’ve written my own scenario with many story cards, added story cards on the fly in existing scenarios, and I freely switch between Do, Say, and Story actions to keep a good flow. It’s engaging and fun to see what the AI does with the information.No AI is without its flaws. There are inconsistencies, and limitations for free users which is fine. I have a bigger issue with the UI, specifically that it tends to bug out frequently. I’ve had UI elements stuck on my screen, buttons that don’t respond to taps until I navigate back or restart the app, sections of UI stuck off-screen, and recently, undoing an action would autonomously redo the same action (needlessly wasting the last of my limited premium actions). I’ve also had some trouble continuing scenarios, returning an error halfway into loading until I restart the app and do nothing else except go *straight* to the scenario.I really enjoy the app. I’m okay with the free user experience, but even in the default Stable build, it’s clear that it destabilizes with use and it’s a little frustrating. I’ll keep using it, but I hope that UI functionality gets a little more TLC.

Gone from good to mediocre at best
07/28/2022
Pokebud10

This app used to be great. It was entertaining, effective, and well-made. It was an amazing way to spend free time. With a series of updates, though, it’s experienced a severe decline. The first of these was the extremely bugged CP protection that while a good idea, was poorly executed to a point that it was several times more likely to trigger on something completely safe than what it was designed to stop. Afterwards was the temporary complete removal of searching through community scenarios, which still has an effect today as a large amount of amazingly made scenarios were permanently deleted. After that was the energy system and now the near-objectively worse 10-input per-advertisement system that makes it feel like it’s made to desperately rake in as much profit as possible. Before these additions and changes (especially in the experimental phases that felt more like a genuine catering to user experience), this app would have gotten a five-star from me in seconds. It’s disappointing to see this program and amazing concept fall from the greatness it was in 2017 or so, and I hope that the miracle of this genuine review from the bottom of my heart as an old player inspires the developers to bring back the more effective and user-first design, or at least make it an option to return to the old AI Dungeon. If not and you, the potential user of a new time, are reading this, better alternatives have been made over the years compared to this depressing shell of a once-great project.

Developer Response

We did implement some filters, and take down some features, so that we could remove 2 very specific types of illegal content and protect our other users.  The features have been restored, and the filters work effectively to block those issues.Regarding ads, did you know that it costs us $500,000 a year MINIMUM to offer this game for free?  AI is an expensive service, and we've done everything we can to maintain our free version for users despite the high cost to Latitude.  This is why we implemented Energy in the first place — we needed to keep the costs under control as some people were using THOUSANDS of dollars of AI calls every day.   We implemented ads as a necessity, and it wasn't a decision we made lightly.  Ultimately we had a choice: end our free-to-play option, or implement ads for free users.  We chose to keep the game free even though we had to use ads because our vision is centered on empowering as many users as possible through AI.  Even with ads turned on, however, we are NOT PROFITING from free players.  Let me make that clear: we do not make enough money through ads to cover the costs of free play.  So we're still in the hole for free play, just not as much as before.  Ultimately, if we want AI Dungeon to survive then we have to keep the ads on. You can make the ads go away, and support the game experience for other players, by subscribing!  We hope you continue to enjoy the game!Learn more on our blog: https://share.voyage/bUpLNXp9xyk
